_comment: 🧩️ BCF 2.1/✳️any's own contribution to the repository test platform — its mutation oracle registration and its declared mutation vocabulary (wave 7, ticket 26/08/23/END-TO-END-TESTING-REFACTOR). A BCF file IS a ZIP of XML markup/viewpoint/snapshot files, and no standalone BCF crate exists in the Rust ecosystem (BCF support only appears bundled inside much larger MPL-licensed IFC toolkits), so the reference here composes the already-linked, genuinely independent `zip` and `quick-xml` crates over the real BCF-XML 2.1 shapes rather than adopting a weaker/unlicensed substitute. Discovered by convention alongside ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio's own top-level manifest; merged into one registry, no central edit required.

oracles.rationale:
🫥️ RECLASSIFIED by the `reimplementation-registered-as-third-party` gate. The crate named here does real work — it parses and writes this format — but what a MUTATION SHOULD PRODUCE is computed by this owner's own `🦀️oracle.rs`. Both halves of the comparison then descend from ONE reading of the specification, so a misreading of it yields two agreeing wrong answers: the single failure a differential test exists to prevent.

The honest split is that the crate discharges "the result is a well-formed file of this format" and NOT "the mutation computed the right answer". Only the second is what a mutation oracle is for, so this is a `cross-semio-implementation` — a required SUPPLEMENT, never a substitute, and a qualifying third-party reference is still owed.

Any fixtures registered alongside are untouched and remain valuable: real bytes of the real format, byte-reproducible, and exactly what a qualifying reader gets pointed at the day one is registered.

📖️ A READER, and that is the whole point of registering it separately.

This subset also carries a `🦀️oracle.rs` that COMPUTES what each mutation should produce. That entry is registered `cross-semio-implementation` and does not discharge anything, because both halves of such a comparison descend from one reading of the specification.

This entry is a different mechanism. The expected state is not computed at all — it is COMMITTED, as the `after` half of a byte-reproducible fixture. `jszip` 3.10.1 then parses the BCF 2.1 zip container on BOTH sides and the comparison is over what it recovered. The probes say so in their own header: "Everything here MARSHALS and READS; nothing here applies a mutation or predicts what one should."

So the judge is a third-party implementation of the format, and nothing in this repository predicts the answer it is judging. That is what makes it qualifying where the sibling entry is not.

comparisonProfiles.description: BCF 2.1 documents compared by version, every topic keyed by guid (title/description/status/priority/labels/creationDate/creationAuthor, comments keyed by guid, viewpoints keyed by guid), and every raw retained part keyed by name by size+content digest. A viewpoint's camera/components project as their full typed structure; its PNG snapshot projects as size+digest rather than raw bytes (an opaque binary payload, not a lossy-encoded sample array, so a content digest is the correct treatment per the fleet brief's raster precedent). Topic/comment/viewpoint/part identity keys make document-order irrelevant; label/selection/exception/coloring lists are unordered sets in the BCF domain, so all arrays compare as sets.
Bundle-style comparison for the jszip+fast-xml-parser oracle: delegates to the bcf-2-1-jszip-compare-v1 pipeline rather than a single-projection diff.

probes.rationale: An INDEPENDENT reader accepts both files at all. Nothing downstream means anything if one of them does not parse.

qualification.evidence: Run against every generated fixture pair this session (15 recipes, 26 files) — bothImport true in every case.

criteria.detail: parses bcf.version + every topic folder's markup.bcf/.bcfv
jszip and fast-xml-parser are both pure-JS, already vendored in node_modules

probes.rationale: The guid-keyed semantic projection every comparison is measured against — version, every topic's fields, comments, viewpoints (camera/components/snapshot size+digest), and every unconsumed raw part.

qualification.evidence: Run against insert-comment-applied/after.bcf: reports topicCount 2 and both comments (comment-01, comment-02) with correct fields.

criteria.detail: topics/comments/viewpoints are objects keyed by guid, matching semantic-bcf-v1's set-comparison rule

probes.rationale: Set/map-keyed deep-equal over two independently-parsed projections — the GATING comparison. Computes no mutation semantics, only structural equality of two already-existing byte blobs.

qualification.evidence: Validated BOTH ways this session with real measured numbers: identical pair -> {equal:true, diffCount:0}; a pair differing in one field (camera fieldOfView 60 vs 999) -> {equal:false, diffCount:1, diffs:["$.topics.t1.viewpoints.vp1.camera.fieldOfView: 60 \u2260 999"]}.

comparisonPipelines.description: Reads the subject's produced bcfzip and the fixture's own expected bcfzip with an independent jszip+fast-xml-parser composition, then compares their guid-keyed projections. GATING.

stages.description: An independent reader accepts both files.
Set/map-keyed structural equality — the operative equality.
